best_for: Java developers and ops teams who need a free, TCK-tested Java 21 with a published support date, especially those already running workloads on Azure.
description:
The Microsoft Build of OpenJDK is Microsoft's own distribution of Java. The company says it runs a great deal of Java itself, from Azure to Minecraft and LinkedIn. It uses the same build scripts as the Eclipse Adoptium project and is tested with Adoptium's quality suite. Microsoft also contributed the Windows on Arm port of OpenJDK.

Install it and you get the full JDK to compile and run Java 21 apps on your own machine. If you deploy in containers, ready-made Java 21 images sit in Microsoft's registry at mcr.microsoft.com/openjdk/jdk, built on Ubuntu or Azure Linux, including a slim distroless version. On Azure, a launcher called jaz can apply JVM settings tuned for the cloud.

points.title: Free OpenJDK, tested against the spec
points.text: It is OpenJDK built and packaged by Microsoft under GPLv2 with the Classpath Exception. The LTS builds pass the Java TCK, so it works as a drop-in replacement for other OpenJDK builds. No license fee and no sign-up.

points.title: Java 21 is covered to September 2028
points.text: Microsoft gives September 2028 as the earliest end of support for its Java 21 builds. Updates ship every quarter, in January, April, July and October. Java 25 is also out, with support targeted to September 2030.

points.title: Paid support only on Azure
points.text: Commercial support is for Azure customers with an Azure support plan, and only for Java running on Azure, Azure Stack or Azure Arc. Everyone else gets community help through Microsoft's OpenJDK repository on GitHub.

points.title: May differ slightly from upstream
points.text: Microsoft can add fixes that are not yet in upstream OpenJDK. Its release notes flag these, and the source code is published.

points.title: Formats for each system
points.text: Windows gets .exe, .msi and .zip builds; macOS gets .pkg and .tar.gz; Linux gets .tar.gz plus .deb and .rpm packages from packages.microsoft.com. All come for x64 and Arm64. There is no Alpine musl build for Java 21, unlike 11 and 17.

points.title: What this page lists
points.text: Here you get machine-wide Windows installers for x64 and Arm64, and macOS .pkg files for Intel and Apple silicon. The Windows listing keeps 16 versions; macOS lists only the current release, so older Mac builds need another source.

points.title: No Java 8 from Microsoft
points.text: If you still need Java 8, Microsoft points you to Eclipse Temurin builds instead.
